test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

When a beggar appeared, / I offered him / an one rupee coin / but he did not take it.

options.text: but he did not take it

solution:
```html
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the article "**an**" before the term "**one rupee coin**."
 
• The article "an" is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. However, the word "one" begins with a consonant sound.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**a one rupee coin**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When a beggar appeared, I offered him a one rupee coin, but he did not take it."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "When a beggar appeared," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "I offered him"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "but he did not take it."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 3.

``
